label: copy-phase input token t (not as first echoed token)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input token is the letter t. It almost never fires on t during the original phase or on any other token (a few tiny activations on n). When t is the first copied token (recall_idx 1, input right after <DEL>, i.e. first_tok = t) it usually stays silent or fires weakly (about 0.55 of max). From recall_idx 2 onward it fires on every copy-phase t at roughly 0.8 to 1.0 of max. The strongest activations (about 0.98 to 1.0) occur late in the copy phase, where the t was near the end of the original sequence. Activation does not depend on which token is being output.

issues: The label and predicate hold up. Test scores are precision 1.000, recall 0.948, F1 0.973, mass recall 0.997. Running misses on the test split found 0 false positives.

The explanation gets the recall_idx 1 magnitude wrong. It says that when t is the first copied token the feature 'fires weakly (about 0.55 of max)'. On the test split the feature is active on only 24% of those steps (precision 0.239), with activations of about 0.02 to 0.05 of max and a mass share of only 0.003. The roughly 0.55 activations in the lowest quartile are at recall_idx 2 (e.g. 'm t j s p g d <DEL> m [t:0.57]'), not recall_idx 1. So 'from recall_idx 2 onward it fires at roughly 0.8 to 1.0' is also wrong: recall_idx 2 gives about 0.53 to 0.57, recall_idx 3 about 0.77 to 0.79, and recall_idx 4 and later about 0.8 to 1.0.

Magnitude rises with recall_idx (how deep into the copy phase the t is), not with where the t sat in the original sequence as such. Top activations (0.98 to 1.0) are mostly at recall_idx 7 or 8, but some are at recall_idx 4 to 6 (e.g. 'q u e t ... <DEL> q u e [t:0.99]'). 'Late in copy phase' is roughly right; 'near the end of the original sequence' only partly holds.
There are no systematic misses: the 4054 missed test steps are all recall_idx 1 t at about 0.03 of max (0.3% of mass). Off-t activations are negligible (dev: 31 on n, 3 on h, 2 on i, 1 on r).
